source_name: Bankar.me – Montenegrin banking and finance trade press
why_relevant: Specialist local-language outlet covering the insurance supervisor, consumer protection in banking and regulatory developments, with topic tag pages per institution. Useful as an early-warning layer and as a pointer to regulator announcements that are poorly indexed on official sites.

source_name: CdM / RTCG / MINA – general Montenegrin news carrying regulator announcements
why_relevant: Mainstream outlets frequently break regulator decisions with concrete deadlines before the regulator's own site is updated (e.g. the Capital Market Authority's T+1 settlement/clearing move from 1 January 2027; AZLP's data-protection handbook launch). Valuable as a deadline-detection tripwire.

source_name: euprava.me service catalogue – institutional identity/contact records
why_relevant: The e-government service catalogue holds per-institution records (address, competences, services) including for the AML directorate and the Anti-Corruption Agency. Useful for resolving official names, successor bodies and current contact points when institutions are reorganised — a recurring problem in Montenegro.

source_name: European Commission — Enlargement: Montenegro country page (annual report / enlargement package)
why_relevant: Authoritative annual assessment of Montenegro's alignment per negotiating chapter, including Ch.4 free movement of capital (AML/CFT, capital restrictions) and Ch.9 financial services (CRR/CRD, DGS, BRRD, Solvency II, payments). Sets the forward-looking conditionality and closing benchmarks that drive domestic banking/payments legislation deadlines.

source_name: Montenegro 2025 Report (SWD(2025) 754 final) — full PDF
why_relevant: The single densest document of forward-looking regulatory obligations for Montenegrin banking and payments: per-chapter alignment verdicts, named directives/regulations still to be transposed, and next-year recommendations.

source_name: ecoi.net mirror of EC Montenegro country reports
why_relevant: Stable third-party archive of EC country reports; useful fallback when EC document-download URLs rotate (they are GUID-based and change per edition).

source_name: wapi.gov.me document download endpoint (Government of Montenegro document store)
why_relevant: Backing file store for gov.me: draft laws for public consultation, accession programme proposals, ministry reports are served as GUID URLs from here. Any monitoring pipeline for Montenegrin regulatory drafts must resolve these links.

source_name: Kancelarija za evropske integracije / Prilozi izvještaju Evropske komisije o Crnoj Gori
why_relevant: Montenegro's own input ('prilog') to the EC progress report — a chapter-structured self-assessment that is often more granular on planned legislation and dates than the EC report itself.

source_name: Central Bank of Montenegro (CBCG) — EU projects / international technical cooperation
why_relevant: Beneficiary-side record of IPA-funded twinning and EU technical assistance on banking supervision and financial-services regulation; names donor partners, workstreams and project periods, which telegraph which acquis pieces are being transposed next.

source_name: Deutsche Bundesbank — EU twinning / Western Balkans central bank programmes newsroom
why_relevant: Lead partner of the EU-funded twinning consortium for CBCG and the multi-ESCB Western Balkans programme; publishes project scope, duration and completion notes that reveal supervisory-convergence priorities before Montenegrin institutions announce them.

source_name: Hrvatska narodna banka (HNB) — twinning with Montenegro communications
why_relevant: Junior consortium partner publishing conference agendas and outputs of the 'Support for regulation of the financial services in Montenegro' twinning — an unusually specific window into which directives are being drafted into Montenegrin law.

source_name: EEAS / EU Delegation to Montenegro — news and press
why_relevant: Publishes EU-side confirmations of milestones with dates (SEPA accession, Growth Plan pre-financing disbursement, enlargement package launch) — the accession calendar as the EU communicates it in-country.

source_name: European Commission — Growth Plan / Reform and Growth Facility for the Western Balkans
why_relevant: The Reform Agenda 2024-2027 attaches money to dated, measurable steps — several in the financial/payments domain (SEPA operationalisation, payment-system modernisation). Payment-request cycles create hard, verifiable deadlines that domestic announcements do not.

source_name: European Commission — Montenegro financial assistance under IPA (IPA III programming)
why_relevant: Annual and multiannual action programmes name the financial-sector/PFM/supervision interventions to be funded, with indicative timelines — a leading indicator of which acquis workstreams get resourced.

source_name: European Commission — TAIEX instrument and events database
why_relevant: TAIEX workshop/expert-mission records are a granular, near-real-time signal of which specific EU acts a beneficiary administration is currently working to transpose. Event listings for Montenegro on financial services would be a high-frequency leading indicator.

source_name: European Payments Council — SEPA geographical scope and scheme participation for Montenegro
why_relevant: The EPC is the gatekeeper of SEPA scheme adherence — its scope decisions, adherence register and scheme rulebook release calendar impose dated compliance obligations on Montenegrin banks independent of national law.

source_name: UNDP Montenegro — regulatory framework assessment for FinTech development (and similar donor diagnostics)
why_relevant: Donor-commissioned gap analyses map Montenegrin payments/fintech law against PSD2, EMD2 and e-IDAS and list what remains untransposed — an indirect but explicit inventory of alignment gaps.

source_name: CBCG — Platni sistem (payment system hub: RTGS + DNS)
why_relevant: Central Bank of Montenegro is owner AND operator of the national payment system (RTGS gross real-time + DNS deferred net). This hub page defines system components, participation model (direct participation only), technical standards (ISO 20022 MX, SWIFT BIC, IBAN, IP/MPLS VPN extranet) and links to RTGS/DNS sub-pages, tariffs and statistics. It is the canonical anchor for the whole cell.

source_name: CBCG — Pravila rada Platnog sistema Centralne banke Crne Gore (payment system rulebook PDF)
why_relevant: The actual participant rulebook: RTGS operating procedures, participant-to-system communication, suspension/exclusion powers of the central bank, cut-off and settlement mechanics. This is the single highest-value document for participant obligations and rule changes; versions of it are what banks must implement against.

source_name: CBCG — Podzakonski akti: Platni promet i platni sistemi (secondary legislation index)
why_relevant: Index of all CBCG odluke (decisions) governing payments: minimum transaction value routed to RTGS, payment-system oversight decision, SEPA credit-transfer/direct-debit conditions decision, fee decisions (e.g. 50% RTGS/DNS fee cut effective 1 December). Best single page to detect new binding acts and their effective dates.

source_name: CBCG — Nadgledanje platnih sistema (payment systems oversight)
why_relevant: The oversight (not operations) side: criteria for designating and supervising payment systems, oversight reports, and the basis on which non-CBCG systems/schemes would be authorised. Reveals whether any private/third-party scheme or switch is formally designated in Montenegro.

source_name: CBCG — Statistika platnog prometa (payment statistics)
why_relevant: Volume/value series for RTGS, DNS and (expected) instant payments, plus card/ATM/POS statistics. Indirect but essential for sizing migration progress and adoption after each mandatory deadline; media cite it (e.g. EUR 2.5bn payment turnover in June).

source_name: Government of Montenegro (gov.me) — public consultation on Draft Law amending the Law on Payment Transactions
why_relevant: The primary-law layer under everything in this cell. CBCG drafted the amendments; the Ministry of Finance ran a 25-day public consultation (announced 15 April – 8 May 2026) that carries the legal basis for SEPA accession, instant-payment obligations and the National Payment Board. Consultation notices give the earliest sight of forthcoming participant mandates.

source_name: Nacionalni odbor za platni promet (National Payment Board / Committee) — coverage and CBCG-hosted material
source_subtype: public-broadcaster reporting on a governance body
why_relevant: The coordination body that convenes CBCG, Ministry of Finance and the commercial banks on SEPA implementation results and payment-infrastructure milestones. Its formation depended on parliament passing the law; its meeting outcomes are where participant readiness and next deadlines get set. No standalone portal was found — currently reachable only via CBCG press items and national broadcaster reporting.

source_name: European Payments Council — Register of Participants in SEPA payment schemes (SCT, SCT Inst, SDD)
why_relevant: Authoritative machine-checkable list of which Montenegrin PSPs have actually adhered to each scheme (SCT, SCT Inst, SDD) and from when. Turns 'Montenegro joined SEPA' into a per-bank, per-scheme readiness dataset — exactly the participant-level view scheme rollouts require.

source_name: European Payments Council — Document library / rulebooks and adherence documents
why_relevant: CBCG signed a licensing agreement with the EPC to import European scheme rules and technical standards for Montenegrin instant payments. The EPC rulebooks, implementation guidelines and their release/effective calendar therefore define the technical standard Montenegrin participants must migrate to, including SCT Inst and the verification-of-payee requirements.

source_name: ECB — MIP News: roll-out of instant payment settlement service in the Western Balkans (TIPS-based)
why_relevant: Documents the multilateral agreement under which Banca d'Italia supplies a TIPS-based instant payment platform to Western Balkan central banks (Albania, BiH, Kosovo, Montenegro), with the platform targeted to operate by mid-2026 and multi-currency settlement. Explains why Montenegro's system is a 'TIPS Clone' and where future cross-border interlinking announcements will surface.
